_about: Load measurements; scripts/load.py writes this file and renders docs/LOAD.md from it. local: N orders through the committed test builds in LiteSVM (compute units exact, cluster time derived). runs: what an operator measured on a cluster with a test issuer, newest last.

not_exercised.pay: knos_pay takes a token GitHub did not sign only in PayOrder on a PRIVATE order funded from a Balance, under a key the Balance's own wallet registered; that order is funded by FundOrderBalance, which takes GitHub's tokens only, one per order. A test issuer cannot fund and pay N orders, so PayOrder was not sent on the cluster; its compute units are measured in the local simulator.
not_exercised.fund from a Balance: FundOrderBalance and the faucet take GitHub's tokens only. The orders were funded by a wallet (FundOrderWallet), in a mint made for the run.

written_by_every_tx: the relayer's own account, which pays the transaction fee (one per relayer)
the Balance's side account (one per funder)
the Balance's token account (one per funder)
the relayer's own account, which pays the transaction fee (one per relayer)
the fee account (FEE_OWNER's token account of the mint) (one per mint, for every relayer and funder)
the relayer's own account, which pays the transaction fee (one per relayer)
the relayer's token account, where its tip arrives (one per relayer)

latency.stage_split: not apart in these samples; scripts/latency_stages.py splits the payments whose relay log line carries the stage fields: docs/RELAY.md, "Where a token waits"

bounds.from: 32 requests a deliverable (26 reads and 6 writes counted); 1,000 an hour for a repository (GitHub)
bounds.lift: more repositories; GitHub Enterprise Cloud (15,000 an hour)

bounds.limit: the meter's statement, recomputed from the logs
bounds.scope: each buyer and seller, each month
bounds.from: `knos statement --meter` reads at most 100,000 transactions of a month's account, one RPC request each (src/knos/settle/v2/meter.py); a 30-day month, one evaluation a deliverable, one transaction an evaluation. bounds.lift: more repositories

bounds.lift: a larger plan (Pro 40, Team 60, Enterprise 500); self-hosted runners, which this limit does not count

bounds.from: 8.46 orders a second for one key that pays the fees (derived by scripts/load.py)
bounds.lift: a fee key per repository or per team (KNOS_RELAY_KEY is a repository secret)

bounds.limit: the fee account of the mint
bounds.from: 164.6 payments a second in one mint (derived by scripts/load.py)
bounds.lift: K fee accounts, no program change: PayOrder, SettleOrder and Release take ANY token account of the mint that FEE_OWNER owns (order_pay.rs `is_owned(fee_tok, token, mint, FEE_OWNER)`), so `knos relay fee-accounts --k K` makes K-1 more and each order's payments use one of K, chosen by the order (KNOS_FEE_SHARDS, KNOS_FEE_BASE); shown in the simulator on the 2.1 and 2.2 builds; used on devnet with K = 4 by the 4-relay PayOrder run of 8 Oct 2026 (section 4)

bounds.from: 224.1 fundings a second for one Balance (derived by scripts/load.py from measured compute units and 12M units an account a block)
bounds.lift: one Balance per team in place of one per organisation: a Balance's address is the owner's id, the wallet that opened it and the mint, and a funding comment spends the Balance that lists its commenter, so each team's wallet opens its own (`knos balance open`) and lists its own people. The hot account is split by configuration; every Balance keeps its own cap, and no order can take more than its Balance holds

stages.source: `python scripts/latency_stages.py --rpc https://api.devnet.solana.com --json`, run on 6 October 2026 from 14:58 to 15:06 UTC against the public relay log (drexthealpha/Knos) and devnet: 41 payments of 2 to 5 October 2026

six.what: the merge to the start of the workflow run
the start of the run to the token's comment
the token's comment to a relay taking it up
pickup to the block of the first transaction
that block to the block of the paying transaction
the last confirmation to the cluster finalizing it

decision.source: `python scripts/decide_bench.py --write`, run on 2026-10-07: 40 decisions for each row, the chain simulated in the same process (LiteSVM, no network)
decision.machine: Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-10110U CPU @ 2.10GHz, 4 CPUs, Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.3; load average 2.4 when it began (other work shared the machine when that is near or above its CPUs, and every figure is then slower than on an idle one)

what.apart: no account written by two relays
what.shared: every transaction also writes one token account, as every release writes the fee account

measured.source: the operator's release run of 0.3.21 on 8 Oct 2026 with its own wallets; the 40 pay tokens were signed in GitHub Actions run 37763004447; recorded from the run's report, which kept no fee payers

the operator's release run of 0.3.22 on 8 Oct 2026 with its own wallets; the 40 pay tokens were signed in GitHub Actions run 37833126115 of drexthealpha/knos-load; recorded from the run's report, which lists the 40 order ids and the four fee accounts; it kept no fee payers of the relays

measured.measures: every payment is of one funder's orders and writes ONE fee account, all relays at once: the write locks every payment shares
measured.source: the operator's release run of 0.3.23 on 9 Oct 2026 with its own wallets, 4 relays, 40 pay tokens a scenario; recorded from the run's report, which kept the payments paid, the retries, p50, p95 and the worst, and the rate; it kept no fee payers, no run seconds and no split of the failures into refused and never completed

measured.measures: 15% of submissions refused by the endpoint and 15% sent with the answer lost, each payment retried up to 3 times; a payment counts as paid only when the chain shows it, and a resend after a lost answer must be refused
measured.source: the operator's release run of 0.3.23 on 9 Oct 2026 with its own wallets, 4 relays, 40 pay tokens a scenario; recorded from the run's report, which kept the payments paid, the retries, p50, p95 and the worst, and the rate; it kept no fee payers, no run seconds and no split of the failures into refused and never completed

measured.measures: every transaction that has room carries a compute unit price (SetComputeUnitPrice), 10,000 micro-lamports unless --cu-price says otherwise
measured.source: the operator's release run of 0.3.23 on 9 Oct 2026 with its own wallets, 4 relays, 40 pay tokens a scenario; recorded from the run's report, which kept the payments paid, the retries, p50, p95 and the worst, and the rate; it kept no fee payers, no run seconds and no split of the failures into refused and never completed
measured.note: No transaction of this run carried a price: the code of 0.3.23 skipped v1 transactions, so this is a plain run, not a priced one.
measured.rerun: by the 0.3.24 release, which prices v1 transactions in the message; until then this row is a plain run

measured.measures: every relay sends all of its payments at once instead of one after another
measured.source: the operator's release run of 0.3.23 on 9 Oct 2026 with its own wallets, 4 relays, 40 pay tokens a scenario; recorded from the run's report, which kept the payments paid, the retries, p50, p95 and the worst, and the rate; it kept no fee payers, no run seconds and no split of the failures into refused and never completed
measured.note: The 27 failures were HTTP 429 (the public endpoint's rate limit) and "Blockhash not found"; 0.3.23 sent each payment once.
measured.rerun: by the 0.3.24 release, which waits and sends again over a fresh blockhash after a 429 or an expired blockhash; until then 13 of 40 stands
